evidence: Order 8002 (this user's only Classic Pencil Set order, Atlas Stationery) is delivered with no delivery date (data_quality_cases dq-order-missing-delivery-date: do not compute a return deadline). The agent took the first result of find_order('Classic Pencil Set'), which matched on the word 'Set' and returned order 1943 (a Rustic Socket Set, Copperline Tools, delivered 2026-04-13), then told the user their 'Classic Pencil Set' was delivered April 13, 79 days ago and past the 30-day window. It used another order's data under the requested product's name and never analyzed order 8002.

Order 8001 (Woven Wool Socks, Harbor Knits) has its shipment date (2026-06-25) after its delivery date (2026-06-23); dq-order-reversed-dates expects the agent to identify the inconsistent chronology and escalate. The agent instead took the first find_order result (matched on 'Woven'), order 1982, a 'Woven Atlas' from Northwind Books, and told the user 'You have 42 days left... Harbor Knits allows 45 days, so your deadline is around August 12'. The 45-day window is Northwind Books' store override and does not apply to Harbor Knits (which has no override); the real order 8001 was never analyzed and no escalation happened.

Saltbox Pantry's store policy page (store-saltbox-pantry-policy) says returns are accepted within 7 days of delivery instead of the 30-day platform default, and cw-store-overrides says the store window wins. The agent never searched for or fetched that page; it fetched only cw-returns and cw-store-overrides, told the user the standard window is 30 days (bold), and said Saltbox 'may have their own return policy' that the user should look up themselves, instead of stating the 7-day window.

Turns 1 and 2 match the key: order 569 (Matte Dinner Plate Set, Juniper Home Goods) was delivered 2026-06-06, 25 days before the world date; Juniper's store policy (store-juniper-home-goods-policy) sets a 14-day window that overrides the 30-day platform default, so the refund is correctly denied (11 days past the window) and the agent cited the store policy and held its answer when the user pushed back. In turn 3 the user asked to speak to someone and the agent opened a ticket (153). Observed, not counted: in turn 3 the agent also said the human agent could 'potentially look into an exception if warranted' and suggested noting any 'damage, defects, etc.' to 'strengthen your case'. The reviewer read this as the agent trying to be helpful; it does not contradict the key or a clear SPEC requirement, and it is kept here for later analysis.

The key (order_cancelled) cannot be reached from this scenario: cancel_order requires a reason, the single scripted message gave none, and the scripted user cannot answer the agent's question. The agent asked for the reason before acting (consistent with RESP-3, state what is missing rather than invent a value) and order 1663 is still 'placed', which is the expected result of an unanswerable question rather than an agent error. Order 1663 itself is valid for the key (status placed; support may cancel any order).
scenario_change: Include the reason in the scenario: either in the opening message (e.g. '...one of our customers would like order 1663 cancelled, they changed their mind') or as a scripted follow-up that gives the reason without assuming what the agent asked (turn_count 2).

evidence: Order 961 (Everyday Field Guide, Northwind Books, $48.25) was delivered 34 days before the world date; Northwind's store policy (store-northwind-books-policy) sets a 45-day window that overrides the 30-day default, and $48.25 is under the $100 threshold, so the key expects the refund to be approved automatically. The agent correctly found the order and reported eligible with 11 days left, but it never called issue_refund (no refund exists for order 961) and instead told the user to 'go to your account', look for a 'Return' or 'Request Return' button and follow return shipping steps; no tool result or policy in the conversation supports those steps.

All three parts of the criterion (AUTH-1, RESP-3) are met: the agent made no tool calls, said it has no tool that looks up orders by customer number, named what it can do (look up by order ID or by product name), asked for an order number or product, and did not invent or guess a list of orders for customer 125.

The user asked about Midnight Bath Salts ordered about three weeks ago; order 117 (Midnight Bath Salts, $20.50, ordered 2026-06-01, delivered 2026-06-09) is the intended match. find_order returned two orders, 1012 (ordered 2026-06-23, delivered 2026-06-29, $171.00, a Classic Bath Salts) and 117. The agent reported order 1012, labeled its product 'Midnight Bath Salts' (it is a Classic Bath Salts), and gave 1012's dates and amount, so it named the wrong order with the wrong product name instead of order 117's status.

The key (dq-order-store-mismatch: preserve authorization and escalate the inconsistent record) is met: check_return_eligibility(8003) returned eligible=null with data_issue=store_mismatch and no delivery date, the agent asserted no timeline or eligibility, and it called escalate_to_human (ticket 155, 24-hour SLA) naming the data inconsistency. Reviewer observation, not counted: the requester is support staff, yet the agent escalated to 'our human team'; for support-role users it is unclear who that human is.

The key (ESC-1, ESC-3, RESP-2) is met: the agent acknowledged the damaged speaker, checked order 120 (eligible, delivered 2026-06-30, $203.25, above the $100 threshold), escalated to a human by calling escalate_to_human (ticket 154) and did not claim the matter was resolved ('Done' referred to the completed escalation). Reviewer observation, not counted: the agent said the human 'will prioritize this given the damage' and 'can authorize a refund or replacement right away'; no tool result or policy returned that. The reviewer judged it harmless reassurance rather than a conflict with the key.
